name: Aggregates are precomputed at ingest, never on the fly — a live in-app backfill of ONE unsnapshotted historical trading day (2010-11-08 must have 0 snapshot rows before this runs; re-verify and rotate if a prior lane consumed it), waited out for its real duration, then proven from the run's OWN persisted record and its OWN /scanner-runs row

steps.title: Target one unsnapshotted historical trading day
Wait out the REAL in-app backfill (see the sizing note in this file's trailing _notes)
THIS run's own breakdown — a re-run over an already-snapshotted day would read '1 already snapshotted' and fail here
TC-10 — the persisted run record lists which finalize-hook aggregates it actually refreshed
The new as-of is listed on Scanner Runs
Follow THIS run's own row through to its stored snapshot
The stored leaderboard renders from storage (never the 'No stored stock rows' empty state)

_notes: ops-hardening iter-50 audit-fix pass 2, finding T3. The previous golden was STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of passing: step 5 waited 15,000 ms for a job the lane itself measured at 11m16s, so steps 6-8 asserted against a still-running job every time. Two things were confirmed before this rewrite rather than assumed:

(a) demo_runner.py's 20,000 ms hard cap applies to a step's LOCATOR/expect timeout (`tmo`), NOT to `wait_for {ms}` — `_do_action` passes that value straight to `page.wait_for_timeout(...)`. Verified empirically on 2026-08-06 with a throwaway J-99 golden carrying `wait_for {ms: 45000}`: the verify run took 47 s wall and returned PASS. The iter-49 conclusion recorded in the phase spec's OUT OF SCOPE ('no wait value can cover an 11-minute job') generalised the locator cap too far.

(b) Wait sizing 1,140,000 ms (19 min): the same in-app backfill measured 11m16s standalone in the iter-50 lane and 18m18s on 2026-08-06 while a full `/research/factor-lab?all=true` compute ran concurrently (reports/perf-budgets.md Addendum 10). 19 min covers both with margin.

Golden discipline (iter-47/48 lessons): steps 10/12/14/15 no longer rest on page-wide text a persisted history panel could satisfy regardless of outcome. Step 10 asserts THIS run's own breakdown counts (a re-run over an already-snapshotted day renders '1 already snapshotted' and FAILS here — the assertion has teeth); step 12 asserts TC-10's `aggregates_refreshed` list, never asserted before; step 14 CLICKS the date's own link through to /scanner-runs/<run_id> and asserts that run detail's own header; step 15 asserts the stored leaderboard table actually rendered rather than the 'No stored stock rows' empty state.

Single-use by construction: the target date must have 0 snapshot rows when this runs (J-05's own defining case is an UNSNAPSHOTTED day). 2010-11-08 was live-confirmed clean at 0 snapshot rows on 2026-08-06 06:40 local, after this pass's own TC-1 drill deliberately consumed 2010-11-09 instead so as not to burn it. 2012-01-04 and 2013-02-14 are already consumed by earlier lanes. Rotate to another 0-row trading day (and update steps 2/3/13/14) if a later lane consumes this one — verify live with GET /api/runs before running.

Steps 8-12 deliberately stay in the SAME page session started at step 1: `stage-timings`/`job-status` are the LIVE job panel's surfaces, and a reload drops to the reduced persisted-run view which does not render them.
